decision: use one literal Unicode simple-fold query type for sidebar search and transcript evidence validation

semantics.matching: locale-independent Unicode simple case folding, no normalization or multi-character expansion
semantics.intentionalChange: sigma variants and long s now match; dotted capital I and i follow simple folding and remain distinct
semantics.literal: escape user input before compilation; no regular-expression syntax in UI
semantics.ownership: application owns DocumentSearchQuery; search compiles once, opened evidence retains its own compiled query across renders
semantics.positions: original UTF-8 byte boundary from matcher, then original-character excerpt; no folded offset mapping
semantics.dependencies: add application direct edge to existing locked regex 1.13.1; no new package/version in Cargo.lock
semantics.unchanged: 160-character query cap, 50-document result cap, worker admission, cancellation, original saved facts, revision/target identity checks

redGreen.service: Greek query returned two rather than three case-equivalent documents before fix
redGreen.reviewFinding: search-only fix found Unicode text but UI lowercase recheck falsely marked evidence stale
redGreen.uiRed: transcript-search-match was not rendered for uppercase sigma evidence
redGreen.green: 7 service tests and 14 targeted GPUI search tests passed; new evidence interaction preserves original package bytes

review.phase: separate call-site review after initial implementation, followed by final diff and focused validation
checks: follow result from service to original transcript and stale check
share exact query construction and matching rule across both paths
escape metacharacters and preserve source offsets
compile outside document/paragraph iteration and rendering loops
keep root switching, cancellation and stale revision checks
verify Cargo.lock adds only application regex dependency edge
review.scope: sidebar search and its evidence view; Agent search not changed
review.performance: remove per-field lowercase allocation by inspection; no measured latency or UI frame-rate claim
